text:
ava: Heads up — since the keystore RBAC change at ~23:10 UTC last night we're seeing a spike in TLS handshake failures between eu-west and ap-south. Not huge but correlated with a deployment window. Sample from edge-proxy logs:

ops-bot: ALERT: 2026-03-20T23:12:03Z proxy/handshake error client=10.4.2.9 server=api-ap-south: tls: handshake failure: cipher suite mismatch (fingerprint 0x9f)

aj: Who made the RBAC change to `keystore-read` roles? I saw a PR but not sure if it was rolled out cluster-wide.

sasha: That was my change — tightened the keystore role scope to restrict cross-region reads. I targeted the staging rollout and then promoted to canary, I did not expect it to touch edge proxies. :grimacing:﻿

kevin: We're also getting KMS denies in the same timeframe. From KMS audit sink: `DecryptDenied: resource keystore/edge-ap-south: action=Decrypt caller=proxy-sa@eu-west`

ava: Putting those together looks like proxies lost permission to unwrap session keys -> fallback to a non-overlapping cipher -> handshake fails. Can we confirm whether the proxies use KMS on-client unwrap or a delegated service?

security-oncall: We use delegated unwrap via keystore-service in the home region. Policy change probably removed `iam:Decrypt` on the service account used by cross-region proxies. Immediate steps: 1) capture full KMS audit logs since 23:00 UTC 2) confirm which service account attempted Decrypt 3) roll back policy if needed 4) open incident ticket. I'll take 1 and 2 now.

jesse: Pasting the quick KMS query I ran: 
```
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_keyring" AND timestamp>="2026-03-20T23:00:00Z" AND protoPayload.status.message:"DecryptDenied"' --limit 50
```
Results show calls from `proxy-edge-eu-west@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` trying to decrypt `projects/redwood/locations/ap-south/keys/edge-session-key` with status `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

aj: That account shouldn't be reaching ap-south keys directly. We route unwrap through keystore-service in ap-south which has the right key ACLs. Sounds like the proxy started calling KMS directly after keystore role denied access.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-20T23:09:41 by sasha promoted keystore-role-change to canary (eu-west, eu-central).

kevin: I ran a quick trace on one failed connection, TLS debug shows cipher negotiation fallback then immediate abort: 
```
ClientHello: supported_suites = [0xc02b, 0x1301, 0x1302]
ServerHello: selected = 0x009f (unknown fingerprint)
alert: unexpected_message
```
That unknown selection is consistent with a wrapped session key mismatch.

security-oncall: Action plan (short):
- sasha: roll keystore-role-change out-of-canary and pause the promotion immediately.
- kevin + aj: collect proxy process envs and confirm keystore endpoint env var.
- jesse: compile KMS audit IDs and link to incident ticket INC-2026-112.
- ava: add a short blameless note in the ticket and tag infra/ops for follow-up on cross-region unwrap path.

sasha: Rolling back canary now. `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deployment/keystore-deploy --to-revision=3` (running). :hourglass_flowing_sand:﻿

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback started for keystore-deploy in eu-west at 2026-03-20T23:18:12Z by sasha.

aj: After rollback I see handshakes drop back to normal within ~2 minutes on a sample of 100 connections. No further KMS denies for that proxy account. :thumbsup:﻿

security-oncall: Confirmed. Closing incident as mitigated, leaving postmortem + action items:
- Prevent direct cross-region KMS decrypt attempts by proxies (enforce keystore proxying in env and network).
- Add a pre-promotion checklist for RBAC changes that includes KMS audit dry-run.
- Add metric/alert: KMS DecryptDenied spikes + correlated TLS handshake failure rate.

ava: Adding to runbook and assigning to infra-security. Link to draft PM: https://go/redwood/runbooks/tls-keystore-crossregion (internal).

kevin: For visibility — attach sample logs to the ticket and include the `cipher_fingerprint` index for search.

jesse: Incident INC-2026-112 created and set to sev-3. I'll own the postmortem and coordinate retrospective.

sasha: Sorry all, I should have checked the keystore consumer map before promoting. Lesson learned.

ava: No worries — good catch and fast rollback. We'll tighten the rollout process. :v:
